players.product: AI colocation in retrofit data centers (NC-1 North Carolina 40 MW IT leased to Nscale; MTL-3 Montreal for Cerebras) plus GPU cloud services on NVIDIA B300 / Vera Rubin clusters

quarterly_data.signal: WhiteFiber's 10-K: besides NVIDIA, Super Micro and Dell, it names Hewlett Packard Enterprise (an official partnership; one of the OEMs through which it purchases NVIDIA servers) and Quanta Computing / Quanta Cloud Technology (QCT, a commercial relationship) among the key suppliers it relies on to secure GPUs, servers and other computing hardware; it received its first shipment of NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 servers from Quanta Cloud Technology in April 2025. It has established purchase orders with leading hardware manufacturers with delivery schedules spanning several months, and multi-quarter purchase commitments for critical hardware such as GPUs, power distribution units and networking equipment.

WhiteFiber's 10-K: MTL-3 (Saint-Jerome, Quebec; approximately 202,000 square feet on 7.7 acres) was developed into a 7 MW (gross) Tier-3 data center for contracted customer Cerebras (5 MW IT load); the retrofit was completed and operational in November 2025, and the site has billed Cerebras CAD 1.4 million (approximately 979 thousand USD) monthly since November 1, 2025 for the duration of the five-year contract. WhiteFiber exercised its purchase option for the site on January 14, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: MTL-3 7 MW gross / Cerebras 5 MW IT load; CAD 1.4 million monthly billing for five years

quarterly_data.signal: WhiteFiber's 10-K: under its Capacity Agreement with Duke Energy for the NC-1 site (Madison, North Carolina, bought from Unifi Manufacturing in May 2025), Duke Energy agreed to use commercially reasonable efforts to provide 24 MW (gross) of service by September 1, 2025, 40 MW (gross) by April 1, 2026 and 99 MW (gross) within four years of May 16, 2025; management believes, based on a Duke Energy preliminary transmission study, that NC-1 may support up to 200 MW (gross) over an extended period, subject to infrastructure upgrades such as new substations. WhiteFiber states that without additional project debt financing it cannot complete the NC-1 retrofit or reach the estimated 99 MW (gross) by May 2029.
quarterly_data.figure: Duke Energy: 24 MW by September 1, 2025; 40 MW by April 1, 2026; 99 MW within four years; up to 200 MW potential

quarterly_data.signal: WhiteFiber's 10-K: DNA Fund (an AI Compute Fund managed by DNA Holdings Venture Inc.) signed an MSA on December 30, 2024 with a purchase order for 576 H200 GPUs over a 25-month period (deployment commenced February 2025; WhiteFiber concurrently placed a purchase order for 130 H200 servers for approximately $30 million), plus two April 2025 cloud services agreements for 104 H200 GPUs (23-month term, deployed May 2025) and 512 H200 GPUs (24-month term, deployed July 2025), raising DNA Fund's total contracted deployment to 1,192 GPUs.
quarterly_data.figure: DNA Fund 1,192 H200 GPUs contracted; 130 H200 servers ordered for ~$30 million

quarterly_data.signal: WhiteFiber's 10-K remaining performance obligations at December 31, 2025: colocation services $926,524,278 (2026: $55,285,668; 2027: $89,923,474; 2028: $91,376,813; thereafter $502,833,948), total contract liabilities $929,697,246. Purchases of and deposits made for property, plant and equipment were $268,402,549 in 2025 versus $79,026,998 in 2024.

connects_to.relationship: NC-1 (North Carolina) AI colocation: 40 MW of IT load leased to Nscale under a 10-year agreement

contracts.signal: WhiteFiber's 10-K: the Master Services Agreement dated November 22, 2025 among Enovum NC-1 Bidco, LLC, Nscale Services US Inc. and Nscale Global Holdings Limited brought a $70.6 million prepayment from Nscale, the main driver of the increase in WhiteFiber's deferred revenue in 2025.
